title: Blowing up a commutator fixed scheme strictly reduces nonabelian inertia
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian regular separated scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth] with a tame generically free action of a finite group $G$, and let $\bar x$ be a geometric point whose inertia group $H\leq G$ is nonabelian. Set $K=[H,H]$, the subgroup generated by commutators $aba^{-1}b^{-1}$. Let $X^K$ be the closed subscheme equalizing every element of $K$ with the identity. The action of $H$ lifts to $Y=\operatorname{Bl}_{X^K}X$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], and for every geometric point $\bar y$ of $Y$ above $\bar x$ its inertia subgroup in $H$ is a proper subgroup of $H$. In particular, if $p:W\to X$ is a maximally dominating $H$-equivariant morphism from a normal scheme such that the ideal of $X^K$ becomes an invertible ideal on $W$, then $p$ factors uniquely through $Y$, equivariantly for $H$, and every geometric inertia in $H$ above $\bar x$ is proper. Maximally dominating means taking generic points to generic points.

source.place: VI Proposition 4.8 and its normal-representation proof, printed p.79; used in VIII 4.2.13, printed p.122 (the reference there to VI 4.7 is the setup of Proposition 4.8). The factorization clause is VIII 2.2.4(i) and 4.2.13.
